subtype: Approach: updating the product and process after the episode [Revision]
passage: Note from the team's coach, after the retrospective on the online complaint. I watched the team of six go quiet at first, then turn practical. Pallavi pointed out that most of the angry posts had begun as messages nobody could find a place to send. So the team agreed three changes: a short form for support linked inside the app, a changelog page anyone can read, and a target of answering every message the same working day. Pallavi sketched the form fields on the board. Anand, the product lead, asked that the changelog also list what was not fixed yet. I asked them to review the reply times in a month. They put the date in the calendar before leaving.

qa.q: What three changes did the team agree?
qa.a: They agreed a support form inside the app, a changelog page anyone can read, and answering every message the same working day.

qa.q: What did Pallavi think was behind most of the angry posts?
qa.a: Pallavi thought most of them began as messages with no place to be sent, pointing to a lack of feedback channels.

qa.q: What other approach could help catch problems early?
qa.a: Someone could read new public posts each morning and pass real issues to the team, so problems are met before they grow.

qa.q: How might a user with a problem see the new form?
qa.a: The user would have a clear place to send it and could expect a same-day reply, so there is less need to complain in public.

grounding: Shows a team adding a support form, a public changelog and faster replies after a public complaint episode.
